scripts/build_synthetic_cube.py is a thin dispatcher: it hardcodes sub='synth' and calls alphacube.cli.main(['synth', ...]), which routes to cmd_synth -> write_synthetic_store. The real generator is make_synthetic_cube/write_synthetic_store in src/alphacube/synthetic.py, not the script itself.

make_synthetic_cube(n_symbols=12, n_days=80, n_minutes=241, seed=0, suspended_frac=0.02, unlisted_days=0, plant_beta=0.0) builds exactly the 8 CUBE_FIELDS (Open/High/Low/Close/Volume/Vwap/Ret/Amt) with cross-sectional beta/market/idio structure and U-shaped intraday volume; suspended_frac marks random (S,D) cells SUSPENDED, but unlisted_days marks OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE only on the LAST symbol's first N days (status[-1, :unlisted_days]), not a random subset.

day_status is stored as a genuine flat (S,D) int8 side-array (day_status.npy) next to the (S,D,M) cube fields, loaded once and cached, and sliced per-chunk by CubeView.tradable_s/_d. This is the only existing precedent in the codebase for a 'daily-only, not per-minute' array living beside the cube -- directly relevant prior art for the new FloatCap/TotalCap/LimitWidth daily fields.

When a test needs the real production grid width or isolation from the shared fixture, it calls write_synthetic_store itself with its own tmp_path_factory dir and n_minutes=241 (the real grid) instead of the shared fixture's n_minutes=24, e.g. tests/test_gp_seeds.py's module-scoped `cube` fixture (8x50x241, seed=5) and tests/test_engine.py::test_kernels_never_write_into_operands (5x40x241, seed=2).

test_engine.py's module docstring states the file's own correctness convention explicitly: references are computed by calling the raw operator kernels (alphacube.operators, e.g. ops.dt_day.day_std) the way a single stock/day/panel would, NEVER by calling CubeEngine a second time as its own oracle. Assertions are np.array_equal(..., equal_nan=True) -- exact bit equality, not np.allclose.

The one deliberate exception to bit-exact assertion is test_panel_to_cube_handoff_and_round_structure, which uses np.allclose(rtol=1e-5) because it compares two DIFFERENT expressions that are only mathematically (not bit-) equivalent due to reduction order.

Chunk-invariance is tested separately from kernel correctness: the same expressions are run under several CubeEngine(chunk_symbols=,chunk_days=) configurations and asserted bit-equal to the unchunked run, including over a random 200-tree population from TypedTreeGenerator(seed=9) with 4 known-broken operator names filtered out; those 4 are pinned separately by a strict xfail.

GPMiner.__init__ creates exactly one random.Random(seed) (self._rng) and hands that SAME object to TypedTreeGenerator(..., rng=self._rng) -- the miner and its generator share one RNG stream, so any new call consuming randomness anywhere in the path shifts every later draw.

TypedTreeGenerator._pick is the single sampling choke point for operator choice: it groups specs by face, calls self._rng.choice(sorted(faces)) (dict keys deliberately sorted first for determinism) to pick a face, then self._rng.choice(...) again within that face. Called from generate, mutate_operator, and _gen/_collapse_leaf's window-selection path.

Verified live: TypedTreeGenerator.mutate_window (221-234) and mutate_constant (236-246) end with `return child if is_valid_root(child) else None` and never call self.acceptable(child), unlike mutate_subtree/mutate_operator/mutate_hoist/crossover which all do. I reproduced this: with banned_substructures={'O:log(F:Amt)'} and e=parse('ts_mean(day_max(mul(log(Amt), 2)), 5)') (acceptable(e) is already False), 200/200 calls to both mutate_window and mutate_constant returned children that still carried the banned key 'O:log(F:Amt)' in one_layer_keys(child); the control, mutate_subtree, leaked 0/200.

Any new hook parameter (scorer registry, generator weights/accept, plugin loading) should get an analogous test.

test_mining.py::test_skip_kernels_reproduces_the_trajectory_until_the_first_refusal is the exemplar for 'per-generation trajectory must be byte-identical up to where a new mechanism actually diverges it': it spies on m.fitness to capture each generation's expression keys, and separately shows that REMOVING an operator from the vocabulary (vs refusing it at evaluation time) diverges at generation 1 -- the right template for testing the new accept(tree)->bool hook.

train.py:62's own comment independently states '29 个严格 0/1 的算子' (29 strictly-0/1 operators) for allow_boolean_ops, matching both design.md's 22-trivial + 7-non-trivial = 29 breakdown and my live registry probe (boolean_output=True count is exactly 29: 22 trivial_boolean=True, 7 trivial_boolean=False). Three independent sources agree on the CURRENT (pre-fix) count.

Live-verified: default_registry().get('in_sustain_stddev') has boolean_output=True, trivial_boolean=True today, yet its implementation computes torch.sqrt(var) over NaN-aware windowed data -- a genuine standard deviation, not a boolean. Root cause: the catalog probe (_probe_constant_capable/_probe_distinct_values) feeds this binary operator's first 'mask' argument a generic continuous random tensor (never exactly equal to 1.0), so the real trigger-match path (`torch.where(mask==1,...)`) never fires and the output collapses to one constant purely as a probe artifact, not a true property of the operator.

The same mask-probing artifact independently affects in_sustain_mean and in_sustain_product (both genuinely continuous: nanmean/prod of windowed data, dt_in.py:820-828,846-859) and, by a related mechanism (the probe's strictly-positive input makes x.bool() true everywhere, trivializing the 'distance to nearest 1' calculation), in_left_one_distance_or_idx and in_left_one_distance_zero (genuinely integer-valued position distances, dt_in.py:608-629) -- 5 operators confirmed continuous/ordinal by direct source reading, all currently misflagged boolean_output=True/trivial_boolean=True.

By contrast, in_is_neighbor, in_no_neighbor, in_sustain, and cross_sustain were checked and are genuinely boolean/indicator-valued by construction (outputs restricted to {0,1}/{0,1,NaN} regardless of input) -- their boolean_output=True flag is correct, not a probe artifact, matching design.md §11.4's explicit list of 22 intentionally-blocked trivial predicates.

result.summary:
Read-only recon of AlphaCube's tests/ directory and conventions, scoped to: tests/conftest.py, test_engine.py, test_expression.py, test_parser.py, test_catalog.py, test_mining.py, test_gp_seeds.py, test_general_call.py, root conftest.py, pyproject.toml, scripts/build_synthetic_cube.py, docs/design.md, docs/HANDOFF.md -- plus targeted, read-only Python introspection (registry probes) and source checks (generator.py, catalog.py, scoring.py, gp.py, cli.py, store.py, synthetic.py, tokens.py) needed to ground the insertion_points and test-case lists precisely. No files were modified; two throwaway probe scripts were written to the session scratchpad only.

Headline results: the full suite is currently clean -- 628 collected, 617 passed / 10 skipped (all 3 optional-dependency gaps: xgboost, tabpfn, matplotlib -- fully identified) / 1 xfailed (a documented, intentional strict xfail) / 0 failed, in 157.48s. My 7 assigned files in isolation: 105 passed / 1 xfailed / 0 failed / 0 skipped in 13.59s.
